title: Trilce: Poem LXXVI — From Night to Morning I Go
text:
From night to morning I go
sticking my tongue out at the mutest x’s.

In the name of that pure one
who knew how to gaze until she became 2.

In the name of her to whom I was a stranger,
key and lockplate so unlike.

In the name of her who had neither voice
nor vote when there was ordained
this fate of hers: to make.

Bubbling of bodies, nonetheless,
fit; a bubbling that always
stood at only 99 bubbles.

Ends, handcuffed in nature,
of two days that never join,
that never reach each other.
editorial_note: The legal idiom of voice and vote is held against erotic estrangement and numerical incompletion; the final remates are rendered as ends to retain both termination and unattainable joining.

title: Trilce: Poem XIII — I Think of Your Sex
text:
I think of your sex.
Heart simplified, I think of your sex,
before the day’s ripened flank.
I feel the bud of bliss: it is ripe.
And an ancient feeling dies,
degenerated into brain.

I think of your sex, a furrow more prolific
and harmonious than the womb of Shadow,
though Death conceives and gives birth
to God himself.
O Consciousness,
I think, yes, of the free brute
who takes his pleasure where he wishes, where he can.

O honey-scandal of the twilights.
O silent roar.

Raortnelis!
editorial_note: Sexo retains its bodily directness while seso turns the spent feeling cerebral; the last word reverses silent roar as Vallejo reverses estruendo mudo into Odumodneurtse.

title: Trilce: Poem XXXIV — Gone Is the Stranger with Whom
text:
Gone is the stranger with whom, late
at night, you returned talking and talking.
There will be no one now to wait for me,
my place laid out, the bad made good.

Gone is the warm afternoon;
your great bay and your clamor; the finished talk
with your mother,
who offered us a tea brimful of afternoon.

All is gone at last: the holidays,
your breasts’ obedience, your way
of asking me not to go away.

And gone is the diminutive, set against
my coming of age in endless grief,
and our having been born this way, without cause.
editorial_note: The repeated se acabó becomes gone is to keep the tolling finality; the grammatical diminutive is opposed to legal adulthood and immeasurable grief.

title: Trilce: Poem XLI — Death on Her Knees Wells Forth
text:
Death on her knees wells forth
her white blood that is not blood.
It smells of collateral.
But now I feel like laughing.

Something is murmured over there. They fall silent.
Someone whistles courage sidelong,
and one could even count in pairs
twenty-three ribs missing
one another, on both sides; count
in pairs as well the whole rank
of escorting trapezius muscles.

Meanwhile, the police snare drum
(again I feel like laughing)
gets its own back and clubs us,
again and again,
from membrane to membrane,
rat
a
tat.
editorial_note: Garantía is translated as collateral to keep its financial and custodial chill; the broken tas con tas becomes an English drumbeat while retaining the staggered typography.

title: Trilce: Poem I — Who Makes Such a Racket
text:
Who makes such a racket and will not even let
the islands left behind make their testament.

A little more consideration
as soon will be late, early,
and better assay shall be made
of the guano, the simple treasure-bearing carrion-stench
offered unwittingly,
in the insular heart,
by the briny gannet to each hyaloid squall.

A little more consideration,
and the liquid topsoil, six in the evening,
OF THE MOST ARROGANT B-FLATS.

And the peninsula rises
by the back, muzzled, imperturbable
upon equilibrium’s mortal line.
editorial_note: Testar is kept as making a testament, while the coined calabrina tesórea becomes treasure-bearing carrion-stench; the guano economy, anatomy, and musical violence remain unresolved.

title: Trilce: Poem XVI — I Have Faith I Shall Be Strong
text:
I have faith I shall be strong.
Give me, one-armed air, give me leave to go
braiding myself with zeros to the left.
And you, dream, give me your implacable diamond,
your untimely time.

I have faith I shall be strong.
Over there a concave woman advances,
colorless quantity, whose
grace closes where I open.

To the air, friar past. Crabs, blockhead!
The green presidential flag comes into view,
lowering the six remaining flags,
all the drapery of the turn.

I have faith in what I am,
and that I have been less.

Come now! A fine first!
editorial_note: Galones hover between braid and rank, rendered through braiding; fray pasado keeps its pun as friar past, and the numerical-political pageant remains deliberately unstable.

title: Who Makes Such a Racket?
text:
I


Who makes such a racket, and will not even let

the islands left behind make their testament.


A little more consideration

as soon will be late, early,

and better assay shall be made

of the guano, the simple treasure-bearing carrion-stench

offered unwittingly,

in the insular heart,

by the briny gannet to each hyaloid

squall.


A little more consideration,

and the liquid topsoil, six in the evening,

OF THE MOST ARROGANT B-FLATS


And the peninsula rises

by the back, muzzled, imperturbable

upon equilibrium’s mortal line.
editorial_note: This separately sourced, differently typeset witness of Trilce I receives the same reviewed lexical decisions while preserving its numeral, spacing, and lineation.

title: Trilce: Poem XLIII — Who Knows, He Is Going to You
text:
Who knows, he is going to you. Hide nothing from him.
Who knows, at dawn.
Caress him. Tell him nothing. He is
hard with all that flees away.
Caress him. Go! How you would pity him.

Tell how it cannot be
that everyone says how good,
when you see him turn and turn again,
an animal that has learned to leave… No?
Yes! Caress him. Do not argue with him.

Who knows, he is going to you at dawn.
Have you counted which pores only let out,
and which let in?
Caress him. Go! But do not let him know
you do it because I beg you. Go!
editorial_note: The poem’s unstable quién sabe is retained as who knows rather than resolved into certainty; imperatives and pronouns preserve the intimate triangular plea.
